title: The mate form of the finite dualizing mixed quotient transition
statement: Under the hypotheses of lem-sf-finite-dualizing-mixed-quotient and n≤m, the images under the level-m scalar-extension hom equivalence of the two sides of the finite dualizing mixed quotient square are equal. This is the transposed exceptional and scalar adjunction square.

source.place: Paragraphs 3-4: transpose the coefficient counit square under the exceptional and scalar adjunctions.

proof.text: Prove the lifted residue coefficient square by quotient induction. On the ordinary etale site, apply the coefficient-chain clause of etaleSingleCoefficientProjection (at ell=0, since it imposes no primality condition) and cancel the base scalar associator. This proves compact-support comparison composition for arbitrary finite coefficient maps. Proper finite coefficient extension and the open scalar isomorphism make the four comparison components used below invertible.

Use the regular-unit composition equation and coefficientCounitMate_cocycle to prove composition of exceptional coefficient counit transposes. Transpose again under the scalar adjunctions. Applying this along both factorizations of the residue coefficient square and cancelling the restriction compositors gives the ordinary etale semilinear square.

Apply the realization restriction-square equation to the coefficient object at level n. Functoriality and naturality transport the etale semilinear square through the four realizations. Conjugate its four vertices by finiteDualizingOrigin. The middle origin inverse pairs cancel and the resulting arrows are the scalar adjuncts of finiteU and integralDualizingExceptionalTransition.

Expand scalarReductionExchange as the mate of scalarRestrictionSquare. Hom-equivalence naturality, the unit equation for mateEquiv.symm, and naturality of the restriction square identify its adjunct with the left boundary of the semilinear square. The right boundary is the adjunct of finiteU_m followed by the L transition. This proves the displayed mate equality without assuming the mixed mate invertible.

proof_origin.place: The quotient-compatibility sentence in paragraphs 2--3, using the proper/open coefficient cocycle, exceptional counit mate calculus, coefficient-only realization coherence and scalar mate naturality.

theorem finiteU_quotient_transition_mate {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) :
    (pbcDerivedScalarAdjunction (integralScalarQuotientSheafMap l E L ι X m)).homEquiv _ _
      ((pbcDerivedExtend (integralScalarQuotientSheafMap l E L ι X m)).map
          (integralDualizingExceptionalTransition l E D X hl h) ≫
        (scalarReductionExchange l E L ι X h).app (integralDualizingFiniteTerm l E D X n) ≫
        (normalizedDVRRes l L X h).map (finiteU l E L ι X D n)) =
    (pbcDerivedScalarAdjunction (integralScalarQuotientSheafMap l E L ι X m)).homEquiv _ _
      (finiteU l E L ι X D m ≫ integralDualizingExceptionalTransition l L D X hl h)
